extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, patent agents, and examiners interacting with CIPO (Canadian patent prosecution)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for filing, examination, notices, national-phase/PCT entry, and related correspondence before the Canadian Patent Office (CIPO). Includes substantive criteria (e.g., priority restoration) and procedural/format standards for Office communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: All business in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: All business related to patent applications and patents before the Patent Office is done in writing: both that which is submitted to the Office or sent from the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This chapter is a guide to notices, letters and requisitions sent from the Office, which encompasses most of the correspondence issued by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner’s notices: action required and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner’s notices require the applicant or patentee to perform an action on or within a time period after the date of the notice. Failure to take the action within the time period will lead to a consequence identified in the Patent Act or the Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (1) If application fee not paid, notice under subsection 27(7) requires payment of fee and late fee within three months; failure results in application being considered withdrawn. (2) If copy of priority document not submitted/made available, notice under subsection 74(4) requires submission within two months; failure results in withdrawal of priority request. (3) If maintenance fee unpaid, notice requires payment before the later of six months from due date or two months after notice; failure results in abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to include in Commissioner’s notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner’s notices are generally structured in a bilingual format and are intended to provide applicants and patentees with key pieces of information to easily identify the application or patent and the required action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical elements: Header identifying notice and plain-language reason; Notice Details (Notice Date YYYY/MM/DD, Application/Patent Number and other references, Fees if applicable, Notice Due Date calculated including extensions for prescribed days); General information (Filing Date, Applicants, Inventors, Title); Text in Body (why sent, what is required, consequence of failure, relevant legal references); Closing Paragraph with manual reference and contact information. Example on due date calculation: time periods counted from notice date and extended to next open day if ending on prescribed day (Good Friday example).

rubrics_metrics.name: List of Commissioner’s notice types and legislative references
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a non-exhaustive list of Commissioner’s notices that can be sent under the Patent Act and the Patent Rules, each linked to the relevant legislative provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: Patent Act: subsection 27(7) Application Fee Not Paid; paragraph 27.1(2)(b) Maintenance Fee Not Paid (Application); subsection 28(2) Filing Requirements Not Met; Patent Rules: subsection 15(4) Translation Required; section 31 Appointment of Patent Agent Required; subsection 74(4) Copy of Priority Document Required; subsections 86(1) Notice of Allowance; subsections 85.1(1)/(2) Notice Requiring Continued Examination; and various PCT-related notices (e.g., subsection 154(7) PCT Applicant Entitlement Notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Courtesy letters: purpose and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Courtesy letters inform clients that a communication and/or a fee has been received and whether it is compliant with the Patent Act and Patent Rules, and may inform clients if their applications are deemed abandoned or patents expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Abandonment letters (formerly notices of abandonment), Appointment of Patent Agent (compliant appointment noted). Structure (bilingual) and fields mirror Commissioner’s notices: Header, Letter Date (YYYY/MM/DD), Application/Patent Number (and previous Commissioner’s notice/date if relevant), General Information (Filing Date, Applicants, Inventors, Title), Text in Body (why sent; reasons for non-compliance if applicable; relevant legal references), Closing Paragraph, Contact information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner requisitions and notices: form and applicant responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner’s reports and notices are unilingual, include a date in the top corner, and an opening paragraph indicating the required time period for response and any requirement to request continued examination. The consequence for non-response is identified in the opening or closing paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The due date for each requisition does not appear on the requisition; applicants must calculate it by adding the specified time period to the notice date. If the time period ends on a prescribed or designated day, time is deemed extended under subsection 78(1) of the Patent Act. See Chapter 2 for time limit rules; see sections 12.04 and 12.05 for more on examiner reports and notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional notice of allowance: structure and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A conditional notice of allowance has a bilingual first page and an unilingual second page listing defects; the due date to respond and the fee owing are indicated on the first page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defects listed on the second page; the notice will include the consequence of not responding and not paying the fee (abandonment). See section 25.01.01 for more information and Chapter 2 for time limits and deemed extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of the right of priority: eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Restoration of the right of priority is a mechanism to extend the time limit for filing beyond the normal 12‑month priority period, limited to situations where the applicant failed to file a request for priority despite due care and/or where the failure was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When acting as a receiving Office, CIPO will accept a request to restore priority if satisfied that the criteria are met; restoration may be effective in designated offices whose national laws provide for restoration. For PCT national phase applications filed on or after Oct 30, 2019, restoration that occurred prior to national phase entry will be deemed restored in Canada upon national phase entry. For regular Canadian applications and PCT national phase applications, applicants can request restoration when filing date is more than 12 months after the priority filing date but within two months after the end of those 12 months. See Chapter 7 for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date of a PCT national phase application
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 161 of the Patent Rules: the filing date of a PCT national phase application is the international filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form to request national phase entry in Canada
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are not required to send a petition to the Patent Office for entry into the national phase in Canada.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The National Chapter of the PCT Applicant’s Guide contains a form applicants may use: 'Recommended Form for request of Entry into National Phase under Article 22/Article 39 of the Patent Cooperation Treaty'. Applicants may use that form to submit national entry requirements and other information.

rubrics_metrics.name: International phase extensions of time governed by PCT rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Act does not apply to international applications during the international phase; during the international phase, extensions of time are available only as provided under the PCT and the Regulations under the PCT (including PCT Rules 80.5, 82 and 82.quater).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed information about extensions of time during the international phase is available in the PCT Applicant’s Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT sequence listing standard requirement (ST.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT sequence listing standard is defined in subsection 1(1) of the Patent Rules to mean Standard ST.26 of WIPO, Recommended Standard for the Presentation of Nucleotide and Amino Acid Sequence Listings using XML (ST.26), as amended from time to time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced as the required standard for sequence listings (see Patent Rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposive construction and claim interpretation principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Purposive construction is performed by the court to objectively determine what the person skilled in the art would, as of the date of publication of the patent application and on the basis of the particular words or phrases used in the claim, have understood the applicant to have intended to be the scope of protection sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Free World Trust and Whirlpool continue to guide the courts; purposive construction principles enumerated in Free World Trust. Note difference between judicial construction (claims adjudicated in court are fixed, result of negotiation with the Patent Office, and benefit from presumption of validity under subsection 43(2) of the Patent Act) and examination (claim language may change during prosecution). Examiners should be 'alive to the possibility that a patent claim may be expressed in language that is deliberately or inadvertently deceptive' (e.g., claiming an 'art' or 'process' that may be a mathematical formula and therefore not patentable subject matter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim date definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'claim date' of a claim in an application or patent is the filing date of the application in Canada, unless there is a priority claimed; in that case the claim date is the filing date of the earliest priority application which supports the subject matter of the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when assessing priority and novelty support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-inflicted wound factor not relevant during examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office does not consider the 'self-inflicted wound' factor to be relevant during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit guidance to examiners that certain theories (used in other contexts) are not applicable in examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple problems/solutions in a single claim vs unity of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should be mindful that identification of multiple problems and solutions within a single claim is not to be confused with lack of unity of invention within the meaning of section 88 of the Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 88 emphasizes that the subject matter defined by the claims are to be linked by a single general inventive concept; multiple problems within one claim does not automatically mean lack of unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of obvious errors during examination
rubrics_metrics.description: During examination, obvious errors should be corrected whenever identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual notes that the courts have addressed the date for claim construction rather than enablement and that obvious errors found during examination should be corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners' searches as ISA governed by PCT requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Searches performed by Canadian examiners as part of CIPO’s obligations as an International Searching Authority are governed by the requirements of the PCT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such searches are not covered by this section of the manual; see PCT rules and PCT practice for details.
